summary: Destructor for a file-stream context object. Frees the copied filename, runs mode-appropriate cleanup ('w' -> sub_5361D0, 'r' -> GuardedFunctionCallCleanup) when a stream object is present, closes the OS file handle under lock unless the TLS error code is 29, propagates a stored negative error code, then frees the write/read/allocator sub-buffers and the object itself.

local_names.lpMem: file-stream context object; lpMem[n] is DWORD-slot n, mode byte at lpMem+92 (0x5C)

operations.description: If lpMem is NULL, return -2 immediately.
If lpMem[20] (this:0x50, copied filename) is nonzero, free it via sub_58AA6F.

If lpMem[7] (this:0x1C, stream object) is nonzero, read the mode byte at this:0x5C; 'w' (119) -> v5 = sub_5361D0(lpMem), 'r' (114) -> v5 = GuardedFunctionCallCleanup(lpMem), any other byte skips cleanup; v2 = v5.
If lpMem[16] (this:0x40, file handle) is nonzero and FileCloseWithLock(lpMem[16]) returns true and *(DWORD*)TLSOffsetGetter() != 29, set v2 = -1.
If (int)lpMem[14] (this:0x38, stored error code) is negative, v2 = lpMem[14].
Free lpMem[17] (this:0x44, write buffer), lpMem[18] (this:0x48, read buffer) and lpMem[21] (this:0x54, allocator pointer) when nonzero, then free the object itself, all via sub_58AA6F.

unresolved: this:0x5C appears in the packet field list as a read; in the visible source it is only the mode byte at lpMem+92. The existing_analysis table additionally maps 0x5C to a decompression read buffer (lpMem[23]); that mapping is not supported by the raw source, so the mode-byte reading is asserted and the buffer claim is left unresolved.
The meaning of TLS error code 29 and the precise free semantics of sub_58AA6F are not in this packet.
The 'w' cleanup sub_5361D0 and 'r' cleanup GuardedFunctionCallCleanup are named from the packet callee list only; their internal behavior is out of scope here.
